title: Finite-Tor domains for iterated relative compact-support products
statement:
Use the finite-coefficient field, ring and operation conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $f:X\to B$ a separated finite-type morphism, and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Suppose an isomorphism of objects $u:Rf_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}A_B$ is given. For $m\geq1$ put $X_m=X^{\times_Bm}$, let $f_m:X_m\to B$ be its structure morphism, and put $M_m=\bigotimes_{i=1}^m L\operatorname{pr}_i^*M$ and $V_m=Rf_{m!}M_m$. Fibre products and projections have the meaning of [def-pc-fibre-product]. For the product $X_{m+1}=X_m\times_BX$, let $\kappa_{m,1}:V_{m+1}\to V_m\otimes_A^LRf_!M$ denote the canonical relative-product construction of [thm-sf-kunneth-relative], formed from compact-support composition, base-change exchange, tensor symmetry and the inverse projection transformations [def-exchange-projection]. Use only these concrete finite-coefficient operations; no duality axiom or unrestricted ambient pro-etale adjoint is assumed. Then $M_m\in D^b_{ctf}(X_m,A)$, $V_m\cong A_B$ and $V_m$ has Tor amplitude in $[0,0]$ for every $m\geq1$. At each inductive stage the two inverse projection transformations defining $\kappa_{m,1}$ are defined and invertible on their finite-Tor coefficient domains: their base coefficients are $M$ on $X$ and $V_m$ on $B$. Thus every $\kappa_{m,1}$ is an isomorphism, and with $\kappa_1=1_{Rf_!M}$ and $\kappa_{m+1}=(\kappa_m\otimes1)\kappa_{m,1}$ the maps
$$\kappa_m:V_m\xrightarrow{\sim}(Rf_!M)^{\otimes_A^Lm},\qquad
u^{\otimes m}\kappa_m:V_m\xrightarrow{\sim}A_B$$
are isomorphisms, with the canonical tensor-unit constraints understood.
